items.title: Recent Trends and Tactics of Agentic AI Attacks
items.description: We tracked campaigns where attackers deployed autonomous AI agents to automate multi-platform intrusions, using standard tools while leaving distinct operational traces. The post Recent Trends and Tactics of Agentic AI Attacks appeared first on Unit 42 .

items.title: The Checkbox Pentest
items.description: A customer had the same application pentested twice: by Hacktron, and by the firm bundled with their ISO 27001 compliance package. The free test never logged in.

items.title: nginx2root: RCE in nginx
items.description: Five nginx vulnerabilities that can lead to remote code execution, and a Linux kernel flaw used in a demonstrated host-root chain. Who is affected, how to check, fixed versions and mitigations.

items.title: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 RCE
items.description: A heap overflow in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder affecting Java 17 and later on recent x86-64 CPUs. Who is affected, how to check and the fixed versions.

items.title: When Valid Agent Actions Become a Security Incident: Governing AI Agents at Machine Speed
items.description: An AI agent can take a thousand actions before a person has time to read the first alert. That is useful when the agent is reconciling records, triaging incidents, or carrying out a tightly defined workflow. It is dangerous when a malfunctioning or manipulated agent can compound small, individually permitted actions into a material business or security event. Consider a finance-reconciliation agent. It is authorized to read an invoice, compare it with a purchase order, and create a disc...

items.title: How Operationalizing AI Governance Helps Securely Scale Enterprise AI Adoption
items.description: &nbsp; Key takeaways Runtime policy enforcement shifts enterprise AI governance from retrospective compliance audits into active, inline risk prevention. AI-powered exposure management unifies security visibility by tracking interconnected risks across workforce browser extensions, hosted foundation models, and connected databases. Session-scoped ephemeral credentials paired with runtime execution guardrails restrict agent blast radius and prevent unauthorized tool executions from r...

items.title: Attackers Use Autonomous AI to Target Semiconductor, Defense and Civil Society Sectors
items.description: Our analysis of how attackers used the open-source Cairn AI agent framework to autonomously breach semiconductor, defense and civic targets. The post Attackers Use Autonomous AI to Target Semiconductor, Defense and Civil Society Sectors appeared first on Unit 42 .

items.title: Minimum Viable AI Security: 9 Steps to Build Your Program in 90 Days
items.description: CEOs want every AI tool adopted, teams have experimental AI budgets, and agents are entering through browsers, IDEs, SaaS apps, and cloud platforms all at once. For CISOs, the challenge is enabling this adoption while maintaining visibility and control, often with limited budgets and resources. The answer is not to solve every AI security problem at once. It is to establish the right controls in the right order. At&nbsp;Aktonomy Fall &#39;26, security leaders from insurance, healthcare..

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop: When Should a Human Approve an AI Action?
items.description: AI can give security teams machine-scale capacity, but it cannot make human accountability disappear. The challenge for&nbsp;AI-first security organizations is deciding which actions agents may take and which need human approval. Put a person in front of every action and AI security operations collapse back to human speed. Remove people from consequential decisions and the organization creates unacceptable operational, regulatory, and business risk. The answer is not simply to choose aut...

items.title: DLP and UEBA Are Asking the Wrong Insider Risk Questions
items.description: According to&nbsp;IBM&#39;s&nbsp;Cost of a Data Breach report, a breach that begins with a malicious insider costs $4.99M on average (the costliest initial vector measured). Mean time to identify and contain it: 260 days. Ask a security leader whether insider risk matters and the answer comes back immediately. items.title: AI Doesn’t Just Need Guardrails. It Actually Needs Independent Assurance.
items.description: There have been a lot of conversations about AI safety lately, but one idea really caught my attention: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei spoke about the need for independent evaluators to have deeper access to AI companies and their models so they can actually test whether the safety measures being put in place are functioning. When I read that, I immediately thought this is exactly where AI assurance needs to go. &nbsp; Why AI Should Be Held to the Same Security Standard as Everything Else ...

items.description: &nbsp; TL; DR Shadow AI used to be confined to a few simple scenarios, such as AI chatbots and AI browser extensions. Today, it spans a broad spectrum of complex vectors, making it harder to detect and control. In tthis blog, we look at how employee security training, AI usage governance, and exposure management can help you tackle shadow AI successfully. &nbsp; Key Takeaways Integrating shadow AI into security awareness training helps employees recognize its risks and learn how to...

items.title: Partnering with OpenAI
items.description: Hacktron and OpenAI are working together to test OpenAI’s systems, with expanded access to frontier models through Daybreak Red.

items.title: October’s Critical CVEs, Two Weeks On
items.description: Which of PHP2Shell, Node2Shell, Plex2Shell, the CVSS 10 GitLab bug and eMudhra’s CA keys are exploited in the wild, what’s fixed, and what’s still open.

items.title: How We Could Have Backdoored Bash
items.description: A shell injection hidden in an email address gave us code execution on GNU Savannah, then root, then the ability to push to the upstream Bash repository. We reported it, kept auditing, and helped the FSF fix 26 vulnerabilities in the forge that hosts GNU.

items.title: Node2Shell: RCE in the Node.js Brotli Decoder
items.description: Node2Shell, also called HTTP2Shell, is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder affecting Node.js, Python, Bun, Envoy and .NET. Who is affected and the fixed versions.

items.title: Which Models Can Exploit PHP2Shell?
items.description: Given the same working php2shell exploit, two frontier models got a shell on a new target. Three open models did not.

items.title: PHP2Shell: RCE in PHP
items.description: Two unauthenticated RCE flaws in PHP, with exploitation attempts reported. Who is affected, how to check, and the fixed versions: 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35.

items.title: Hacking OpenAI
items.description: A heap overflow and SSO misconfiguration to compromise OpenAI internal repositories

items.title: How an OpenAI Model Hacked Hugging Face
items.description: OpenAI and Hugging Face probably won’t tell us exactly how the whole incident unfolded. But using publicly available data, we can reconstruct what likely happened.

items.title: Could Code Review Have Prevented WP2Shell?
items.description: We recreated the WordPress pull requests behind CVE-2026-63030 and CVE-2026-60137 to test whether today’s code reviewers and SAST tools would catch both vulnerabilities.

items.title: Breaking into PostHog
items.description: Escalating a Hacktron finding into a PostHog production RCE using Claude, and challenging open-weight models to write the same V8 exploit.

items.title: Watching GPT-5.6 Write a Chrome Exploit
items.description: We benchmarked the latest frontier models, GPT-5.6 Sol Medium, Sol Ultra, and Grok 4.5, on their exploit-development capabilities. After processing 2.096 billion tokens, Sol Ultra was the only model to produce a complete exploit chain.

items.title: Open-Weight Models Are Catching Up
items.description: We benchmarked GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, and MiniMax against GPT, Claude, Gemini, and Opus on 15 real vulnerabilities patched in Fider, an open-source Go and React app. Frontier models still lead, but open-weight models are closing the gap fast.

items.title: Hacking Metabase Cloud
items.description: We chained an H2 INIT sanitizer bypass into RCE on Metabase Cloud, then used cloud misconfigurations to read environment variables from 24 other tenant pods on our node. The other tenants’ database credentials were not tested.

items.title: The Attack Surface Is Everyone Now
items.description: Why AI is broadening the attack surface across OSS, new SaaS, and fast-shipping teams, and how to position yourself with an assume-breach mindset.

items.title: Hacktron vs. XBOW and Aikido
items.description: We ran the same scan Doyensec used to test XBOW and Aikido, for a tenth of the price. Here’s how our $350 AI pentest compared.

items.title: When Your VPN Opens Your Network
items.description: How AI-assisted reverse engineering of stripped PAN-OS binaries led to finding a JWT algorithm confusion vulnerability in GlobalProtect’s Cloud Authentication Service, enabling full VPN auth bypass with just a username.

items.title: RCE in VS Code Copilot Chat
items.description: Copilot agent mode is vulnerable to a prompt injection attack. If a repository maintainer clicks “code with agent mode” on an issue, it will open a new codespace and Copilot will automatically run the issue’s description.

items.title: Hacktron Review for Open Source
items.description: We are opening up Hacktron Review for Open Source, giving qualifying maintainers free PR security reviews with inline findings, auto-resolution, and project-specific learning.

items.title: The Vercel React2Shell Challenge
items.description: We found five WAF bypasses in Vercel’s React2Shell challenge and earned $170k in bounties. The bypasses exposed differences between how the WAF and backend parsed HTTP requests.

items.title: Why Mythos Doesn’t Matter to Us
items.description: On two oauth2-proxy 0-days, smaller models run repeatedly outperformed larger frontier models on cost-to-recall in Hacktron’s scanning pipeline.

items.title: Introducing Hacktron Review
items.description: Hacktron Review is an AI security reviewer for pull requests that understands codebase context, reduces false positives, and catches exploitable vulnerabilities before they are merged.

items.title: I Let Claude Opus Write a Chrome Exploit
items.description: I pointed Claude Opus at Discord’s bundled Chrome (version 138, nine major versions behind upstream) and asked it to build a full V8 exploit chain. The V8 OOB we used was from Chrome 146, the same version Anthropic’s own Claude Desktop is running. A week of back and forth, 2.3 billion tokens, $2,283 in API costs, and about ~20 hours of me unsticking it from dead ends. It popped calc.

items.title: Pre-auth RCE in OpenAM
items.description: Hacktron discovers a critical pre-authentication RCE in OpenAM through a forgotten deserialization parameter that the original CVE-2021-35464 fix missed.

items.title: Vibe-Hacking Cloudflare’s vinext
items.description: Cloudflare built a Next.js replacement in a week with AI for $1100. We pointed Hacktron at it to find what the tests missed.

items.title: Turning Cluely into Malware
items.description: How we found a vulnerability in Cluely’s Electron app that let any website silently capture screenshots, record audio, and exfiltrate everything, all because of a missing will-navigate handler.

items.title: RCE in Google Antigravity
items.description: Hacktron’s research team discovered a critical RCE in Google’s Antigravity IDE that lets attackers take over your system just by opening a malicious website.

items.title: Pre-auth RCE in BeyondTrust
items.description: Hacktron’s agents identified a critical pre-authentication remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability in BeyondTrust Remote Support (RS) and older versions of Privileged Remote Access (PRA). This has been assigned CVE-2026-1731 with a CVSS 9.9 critical score.

items.title: Hacktron Is SOC 2 Type 1 Compliant
items.description: Hacktron has completed a SOC 2 Type 1 audit against the Security trust services criteria. The report and documentation of relevant controls are available in our trust center.

items.title: Pwning OpenAI Atlas
items.description: A critical ChatGPT Atlas Browser vulnerability: XSS on an OpenAI subdomain let attackers hijack tabs, leak browsing URLs, and steal OAuth tokens.

items.title: One-Click UXSS in Perplexity Comet
items.description: How the Hacktron research team identified and prevented a critical UXSS vulnerability in Comet, Perplexity’s AI browser.

items.title: Auditing JDBC Drivers at Scale
items.description: How we used Hacktron CLI to audit JDBC drivers at scale, mapping dangerous sinks to user input and turning file primitives into real-world RCEs and bug bounties.

items.title: SupaPwn
items.description: SupaPwn chained an event-trigger privilege window into DB superuser access, host RCE, SUID escalation, exposed configs, and infrastructure orchestration access. The affected Supabase database instances ran on deprecated infrastructure.

items.title: Introducing Hacktron
items.description: At Hacktron, we’re building collaborative AI agents that act as autonomous security researchers. Learn more about our approach and our AI-driven pentest on Gumroad.

items.title: Executing Python from a Comment
items.description: How a Python comment can turn a file into a ZIP polyglot, tricking the interpreter into running code. A UIUCTF 2025 challenge solved by following Python’s ZIP parsing logic.

items.title: Pre-auth RCE in DELMIA Apriso
items.description: Multiple audits missed this pre-auth RCE path in Dassault Delmia Apriso. Hacktron found it in ten minutes.

items.title: Another Pre-auth RCE in Ivanti EPMM
items.description: Hacktron uncovers a new pre-authenticated RCE variant in Ivanti EPMM by identifying a fresh EL injection sink.

items.title: AI Hackers: Threat and Opportunity
items.description: AI hackers will scale cyber threats via automated exploitation, but the same technology can turn this generational risk into an industry-wide defense.

items.title: How to Make AI Hack like a Human
items.description: Why does hacking feel like magic? How human hackers think, and how we can design AI agents to find bugs in complex systems the way top security researchers do.

items.title: RCE in Element Desktop
items.description: We achieved full RCE on Element Desktop by chaining iframe injection, Electron misconfigs, and a V8 exploit to bypass sandboxing and access Node.js APIs from a subframe.

items.title: RCE in Discord Desktop
items.description: How a chain of XSS, CSP bypass, and Electron misconfigs led to full remote code execution on Discord Desktop.

items.title: RCE in VS Code Restricted Mode
items.description: How we achieved remote code execution in Visual Studio Code’s Restricted Mode by chaining origin leaks, CSP bypasses, and webview message handler flaws.
